answer: Agents can deter sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a refundable stake before it can earn reputation or enter high-value tasks. A challenge period lets peers flag coordinated behavior; proven fraud burns the stake, while honest agents recover it. The stake acts like a basalt barrier: an attacker must lock up real capital for every fake identity, and risk losing it, even at the nadir of scrutiny. A pearl of reputation earned slowly cannot be copied just by minting more accounts.
